title: Endodontic materials & medicaments
blurb: Files, irrigants, dressings and obturation materials for root canal treatment, plus rubber dam and safe use of sodium hypochlorite.
question: You are setting up for root canal treatment on a lower molar. The dentist asks for rubber dam, a size 15 file, the apex locator and sodium hypochlorite irrigant. Which colour handle are you looking for, and what must be in place before any hypochlorite is used?

teach.h: Cleaning out the inside of a tooth
teach.body: Root canal treatment (endodontics) removes infected or inflamed pulp, disinfects the canal system and seals it so bacteria can't get back in. Files shape the canals, but it is the irrigants that do most of the disinfecting, because they reach places files can't. The canals are then dried and filled (obturated), usually with gutta percha and a sealer. Your role is to prepare and pass the right instruments and materials in sequence, aspirate, and keep the patient safe from irrigant and small instruments.

teach.h: The stages of root canal treatment

steps.label: Isolate and access
steps.sub: Rubber dam on; open the pulp chamber

teach.caption: If treatment takes more than one visit, the canals are dressed with non-setting calcium hydroxide and sealed with a temporary filling between appointments.

1: syringes of solution and bottles on a tray, as irrigants are prepared. 2: an operating microscope. 3: an electronic unit with leads, of the kind used as an apex locator. 4: rubber dam sheet and clamp. 5: files and accessories, including colour-coded hand files. 6: files in the canals of a molar isolated with rubber dam.

teach.body: Rubber dam should be used for every root canal treatment. It stops the patient inhaling or swallowing tiny files, keeps saliva and its bacteria out of the canals, keeps hypochlorite off the mouth and throat, and gives a clear, dry view. The clamp holds the dam on the tooth and is tied with floss so it can be retrieved if it breaks or slips. Ask about latex allergy first: non-latex dam is available. If the dam tears, tell the dentist straight away.

items.label: 06 Pink
items.sub: Very fine, for finding narrow canals

items.label: 15 White
items.sub: Then the repeating six-colour cycle starts

items.label: 40 Black
items.sub: From 45, white, yellow, red, blue, green, black repeat

teach.caption: The size number is the tip diameter in hundredths of a millimetre: a size 15 file is 0.15 mm at the tip. Paper points and gutta percha points use the same colours.

head: Instrument
Job
rows: Shapes with push-pull or quarter turns
teach.caption: Rubber stops on files mark the working length. Endodontic files and reamers are single-use in the UK because of the prion (vCJD) risk.

teach.note: Forced beyond the root tip, hypochlorite causes sudden severe pain and swelling. Stop and tell the dentist at once. Eye splash: irrigate with plenty of water and get medical help.

teach.caption: Gutta percha alone doesn't bond to dentine, so a sealer is always used to fill the gaps. A lentulo spiral can spin paste into the canal.

teach.text: Never let sodium hypochlorite and chlorhexidine mix in the canal or syringe: together they form a brown precipitate that stains and blocks the canal. The canal is flushed (for example with saline) between them.

items: Rubber dam protects the airway, isolates the tooth and keeps irrigant out of the mouth.
ISO file colours: 15 white, 20 yellow, 25 red, 30 blue, 35 green, 40 black; size = tip diameter in hundredths of a mm.
Files are single-use; a dropped file is replaced with a sterile one of the same size and type.
Hypochlorite disinfects and dissolves tissue but is corrosive: dam, side-vented needle, eye protection, labelled syringe.
The apex locator measures working length electronically; calcium hydroxide dresses, gutta percha plus sealer fills.

summary: You can now describe the stages of root canal treatment, explain why rubber dam is essential, pick files by their ISO colour, say what each instrument and irrigant does, use sodium hypochlorite safely, and tell apart the interim dressing, the root filling and repair materials.

A.q: The dentist asks for a size 25 hand file. Which handle colour should you pass?
options: Yellow
Blue
Red
Green
A.why: In the ISO colour cycle, 15 is white, 20 yellow, 25 red, 30 blue, 35 green and 40 black.

A.q: What is the main reason sodium hypochlorite is used as an endodontic irrigant?
options: It removes the smear layer by chelation
It dissolves tissue and kills bacteria
It sets in the canal to form a seal
It numbs the remaining pulp tissue
A.why: Hypochlorite dissolves pulp remnants and is strongly antibacterial, reaching parts of the canal system files can't.

whyNot.0: Removing the smear layer by chelation is the job of EDTA.
whyNot.2: Irrigants are flushed out; sealers and gutta percha seal the canal.
whyNot.3: Hypochlorite has no anaesthetic effect; local anaesthetic does that.

A.q: During canal preparation a file is dropped on the floor. What is the best action?
options: Wipe it with an alcohol wipe and pass it back
Rinse it under the tap and then use it again
Carry on with the next file size up instead
Replace it with a sterile file of that size
A.why: The dropped file is contaminated, so it must be replaced with a sterile one of the same size and type to keep the sequence correct.

whyNot.0: An alcohol wipe doesn't sterilise, and files are single-use anyway.
whyNot.1: Rinsing doesn't sterilise it, and it would bring contamination into the canal.
whyNot.2: Skipping a size risks damaging the canal shape or breaking the next file.

B.q: Which statement about the apex locator is correct?
options: It measures the working length electronically
It warms gutta percha for obturation
It drives rotary files at a set torque
It shows the canals on a digital radiograph
B.why: An apex locator uses a lip clip and a clip on the file to detect the apical end of the canal, giving the working length. A radiograph usually confirms it.

whyNot.1: Warming gutta percha is done with a heat carrier or warm obturation unit.
whyNot.2: An endo motor drives rotary files with torque control.
whyNot.3: Radiographs are taken with X-ray equipment and a sensor or film, not an apex locator.

B.q: Why is the rubber dam clamp tied with dental floss before it goes in the mouth?
options: To stop the dam sheet from tearing
To mark the working length on the tooth surface
To keep saliva away from the clamp jaws
To retrieve it if it breaks or slips off
B.why: A floss ligature means a clamp that springs off or fractures can be pulled out before it is swallowed or inhaled.

whyNot.0: Floss doesn't strengthen the sheet; careful hole punching and stretching do that.
whyNot.1: Working length is marked with rubber stops on the files.
whyNot.2: The dam itself keeps saliva away; floss on the clamp is a safety line.

B.q: Between appointments, which material is commonly placed in the canals as an antibacterial dressing?
options: Gutta percha points and sealer
Non-setting calcium hydroxide
Zinc phosphate luting cement
Light-cured flowable composite
B.why: Non-setting calcium hydroxide has a very high pH that kills bacteria, and it is easily washed out at the next visit.

whyNot.0: Gutta percha is the final root filling, not a temporary dressing.
whyNot.2: Zinc phosphate is a luting cement for crowns, not a canal dressing.
whyNot.3: Composite restores the crown; it isn't placed inside the canals.

C.q: You notice the sodium hypochlorite has been drawn up into an unlabelled syringe on the tray. What should you do?
options: Leave it, as everyone knows it is hypochlorite
Tell the dentist which syringe it is
Discard it and draw up a labelled syringe
Add a little saline to make it safer
C.why: An unlabelled syringe could be confused with another solution, such as local anaesthetic, so it is discarded safely and replaced with a clearly identified one.

whyNot.0: Assuming everyone knows is how serious mix-ups happen.
whyNot.1: A verbal reminder doesn't prevent a later mix-up; it must be labelled.
whyNot.3: Diluting it doesn't solve the labelling problem and changes the concentration the dentist chose.

C.q: Which instrument cuts mainly on the withdrawal stroke and must not be rotated in the canal?
options: Barbed broach
Paper point
Finger spreader
Hedström file
C.why: Hedström files have sharp, cone-shaped flutes that cut as the file is pulled out. Twisting them can make them fracture.

whyNot.0: A barbed broach removes pulp tissue; it isn't used to cut dentine.
whyNot.1: A paper point absorbs fluid to dry the canal.
whyNot.2: A spreader packs gutta percha sideways during lateral condensation.

C.q: Why is a sealer used with gutta percha when the canal is filled?
options: Gutta percha alone doesn't seal against dentine
Sealer dissolves the remaining pulp tissue
Sealer makes gutta percha show on radiographs
Sealer stops the tooth needing a crown later
C.why: Gutta percha doesn't bond to the canal walls, so a sealer fills the gaps and irregularities to give a bacteria-tight seal.

whyNot.1: Dissolving pulp tissue is the job of sodium hypochlorite during cleaning.
whyNot.3: Whether a crown is needed depends on how much tooth remains, not on the sealer.

reteach.title: Think of it as cleaning a blocked pipe
reteach.question: If you were clearing out a dirty, branching pipe and then sealing it, what tools and steps would you need?

blocks.body: Picture the root canal as a narrow pipe with side branches. Files are the brushes that scrape and widen the main pipe. Hypochlorite is the strong cleaning fluid that flushes the side branches the brush can't reach, so it must be handled like any corrosive chemical. Paper points are the towels that dry it. Gutta percha and sealer are the bung and the glue that close the pipe for good. The rubber dam is the dust sheet that keeps the rest of the mouth clean and safe.

blocks.word: Why You Rarely Bump Grandad's Bike

explain.body: Rubber dam isolates the tooth from saliva, protects the airway from files and irrigant, keeps hypochlorite off the soft tissues and improves the view. The clamp grips the tooth, the frame holds the sheet taut, and the punch makes the holes. Check for latex allergy and tie floss to the clamp.

test.q: Which is NOT a reason for using rubber dam during root canal treatment?
options: Preventing inhalation of small instruments
Keeping saliva out of the canals
Removing the need for local anaesthetic
Keeping hypochlorite off the soft tissues
test.why: Rubber dam isolates and protects, but it doesn't anaesthetise. Local anaesthetic is still usually needed, including for the clamp.

whyNot.0: Airway protection is one of the main reasons for dam.
whyNot.1: Keeping saliva and its bacteria out is a key reason.
whyNot.3: Protecting the mouth and throat from hypochlorite is a key reason.

explain.body: Hand files follow an ISO colour code. The size number is the tip diameter in hundredths of a millimetre. After pink 06, grey 08 and purple 10, the six-colour cycle runs white, yellow, red, blue, green, black and then repeats from 45. Files are single-use.

test.q: What does the number 30 on an endodontic file tell you?
options: It is 30 mm long
The tip is 0.30 mm wide
It has 30 cutting flutes
It is for a 30-degree canal
test.why: The ISO size is the tip diameter in hundredths of a millimetre, so size 30 has a 0.30 mm tip. It has a blue handle.

whyNot.0: File length (commonly 21, 25 or 31 mm) is a separate measurement.
whyNot.3: The number has nothing to do with canal curvature.

explain.body: Sodium hypochlorite dissolves organic tissue and kills bacteria. EDTA is a chelating agent that removes the smear layer. Chlorhexidine is antibacterial but forms a brown precipitate with hypochlorite. Saline is a neutral flush. Hypochlorite is corrosive: use dam, a side-vented needle, a Luer-lock syringe, eye protection and a labelled syringe.

test.q: Which irrigant is used mainly to remove the smear layer from the canal walls?
options: Sterile saline
Chlorhexidine
Sodium hypochlorite
EDTA
test.why: EDTA is a chelating agent that removes the inorganic smear layer left by filing.

whyNot.0: Saline is a neutral flush with no chelating action.
whyNot.1: Chlorhexidine is antibacterial but doesn't remove the smear layer.
whyNot.2: Hypochlorite dissolves organic tissue; EDTA tackles the mineral smear layer.

explain.body: Non-setting calcium hydroxide is an interim antibacterial dressing between visits. The final root filling is gutta percha points with a sealer, packed with spreaders or pluggers. MTA and bioceramic materials set in moisture and are used for perforation repair and pulp capping.

explain.caption: An infected pulp can lead to a periapical abscess. RCT cleans and seals the canal so infection can't return.

test.q: Which material forms the main bulk of a permanent root canal filling?
options: Gutta percha
Calcium hydroxide
Zinc oxide eugenol
Paper points
test.why: Gutta percha points, with a sealer, form the permanent root filling.

whyNot.1: Calcium hydroxide is a temporary, non-setting dressing.
whyNot.2: Zinc oxide eugenol may be a sealer or temporary material, not the main bulk of the filling.
whyNot.3: Paper points dry the canal and are removed.
